cases.sentence: Ну, это очень просто: на ___, черной тушью, рисуются две оси – одна ось горизонтальная, другая вертикальная.
cases.explain: «веленевой бумаге» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Shall I tell you what kind of individualized charts they were? Now, that’s simple: on white vellum in black India ink I drew two axes, one horizontal, the other vertical. All the workdays of the previous month were indicated sequentially on the horizontal axis, the amount of alcohol consumed—<calculated on the basis of degree of proof—on the vertical axis. Of course, only whatever was consumed on the job or before was tabulated, since the amount consumed in the evening remained relatively constant, and was, therefore, of little interest to a serious re- searcher.

cases.sentence: А я, черной тушью и на ___, изображаю все это красивою диаграммою.
cases.explain: «веленевой бумаге» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Thus at the end of the month the worker came to me with his report: on such and such a day, such and such an amount of such and such consumed, on another day so much of whatever. While I would illustrate all of that with a beautiful graph in black India ink on white vellum. Here, for you to admire, for instance, is the chart for Viktor Totoshkin, member of the Komosomol: 100 26th

cases.sentence: А вот уж это – ваш ___, экс-бригадир монтажников ПТУСа, автор поэмы «Москва – Петушки»:
cases.explain: «покорный слуга» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: And here we have your faithful servant, ex-head cable- fitter and author of the poem Moscow to the End of the Line: 100 10th 26th

cases.explain: «интересные линии» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Aren’t these truly interesting graphs? Interesting even to the most superficial eye? They looked variously like the Himalayas, the Tyrol, oil derricks, or even the Kremlin wall, which, admittedly, I have never seen. Another one looked like a morning breeze on the Kama River, a gentle splash with rippling beads of lantern light. Still someone else’s was like the beating ofa proud heart, the song of the stormy petrel—in other words, pure Gorky—or like Aivazovsky’s trashy painting of the ninth wave. And all this, only looking at the external form of the line.

cases.sentence: А тому, кто пытлив (ну вот мне, например), эти линии выбалтывали все, что только можно выболтать о человеке и о ___: все его качества, от сексуальных до деловых, все его ущербы, деловые и сексуальные.
cases.explain: «человеческом сердце» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: But, for anyone inquisitive (me, for instance), the lines blurted out everything that was possible to blurt out about the man and the heart of the man—all his qualities, from sexuality to practical matters as well as all his faults, both sexual and practical. Also, the degree of steadiness of temperament and of the tendency to treachery plus all his unconscious secrets, if he had any unconscious secrets.

cases.sentence: Но не очень долго рассматривал: в один ___ у меня со стола исчезли все мои диаграммы.
cases.explain: «злосчастный день» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: I then examined with care, intently and close up, the soul of every shitass. But I didn’t examine them for long—one fateful day all the charts disappeared from my desk. It seems that, on the same day, the old fogy Aleksei Blindiaev, member of the CPSU since 1936, sent off to the Administrative Section our obligatory holiday projec- tion, in which we all swore, on the occasion of the upcoming Centennial, to be the same in our everyday life as at work. And, perhaps out of foolishness or perhaps drunkenness, he put my individualized charts into the same envelope.
